chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'O Muhammad! People will not cease to engage in discourse until they speak about God. So when you hear that, say: There is no god except God, the One, Who there is nothing like unto Him.'

key_terms.التنزيه: tanzih — the theological concept of God's absolute transcendence and incomparability to creation
key_terms.الْمَنْطِقُ: discourse/speculation — in this context refers to philosophical or theological speculation about God's nature
key_terms.الْوَاحِدُ: the One — a divine name emphasizing absolute unity (tawhid)
key_terms.كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ: nothing like unto Him — the principle of divine incomparability (tanzih), drawn from Quran 42:11

ai.seo_question: What should Muslims say when they hear people speculating about God's nature?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) warns his companion Muhammad ibn Muslim that people will inevitably engage in speculative theological discourse about the nature of God. He instructs that when one encounters such speculation, the correct response is to affirm divine unity with the formula of tawhid: 'There is no god except God, the One, Who there is nothing like unto Him.' This teaching reflects the Shia theological position that speculation about God's essential nature (kayfiyya) is discouraged, and that the affirmation of God's absolute oneness and incomparability (tanzih) is the proper response to theological overreach.
